_note: Keys the ledger must not count as unread, each with the reason. Prefix form '<endpoint> <sub>.*' covers a sub-object. A decision is an allowance: it needs a reason a reviewer can check, and the test refuses one that names a key no fixture carries.
iterated: Story.tsx passes the whole object to TermGroup / Object.entries
/api/stats/session/{gaming_session_id}/d: debug block for operators, not a datapoint for a visitor
/api/stats/last-session scoring.debug: debug block for operators, not a datapoint for a visitor
/api/stats/session/{gaming_session_id}/d: retired on purpose: a literal copy of played_pct (sessions_router.py:2203-2204, BACKLOG 2026-09-03); alive_pct_lua and alive_pct_diff are NOT copies (engine TAB[8] vs computed) and stay unread
/api/live/state server_time: transport field (the server's clock for the poll), not a datapoint
/api/stats/last-session map_counts.*: data-map: the keys are map names (a table of counts by map), not fields
/api/storytelling/kill-impact entries.*: duplicate: `entries` is the same list as `players` (kis.py serves both names for the legacy page); the Story page reads `players`
/api/players/{identifier}/card percentil: iterated: PlayerCardSection prints every percentile through Object.entries, so the pool's keys are not named in the source
/api/greatshot/{demo_id} highlights.clip: the server path of the cut clip; clip_download is built from the same row, so the path is the link's title and never a state of its own (Codex on #1003)
/api/proximity/event/{event_id} round_en: the round's end wall time; the page prints the canonical round_duration_seconds instead of end − start, which includes pauses and reads 0:00 on zero sentinels (Codex on #1004)
/api/proximity/summary v5_counts.*: iterated: Object.entries prints every source table's row count under 'v5 source rows in this scope' (ProximityOutcomes)
/api/proximity/competitive/wave-cycles c: iterated: Object.entries draws a ClockBadge per team with every field (ProximityRoundCanvases)
/api/proximity/events events.reaction_ms: an alias: get_proximity_events sets reaction_ms and duration_ms from the same column (row[6]); combat_engagement has no reaction column, the drill-down's attackers carry first_hit_ms (Codex on #1010)
